question: In which year was A. P. J. Abdul Kalam honoured with the Bharat Ratna?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1997.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A. P. J. Abdul Kalam was honoured with the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in the year 1997.

• He received it for his contribution to India's missile and space programmes while serving as a scientist and science administrator.

• The award (भारत रत्न) is conferred for exceptional service towards advancement of art, literature, science and public service.

• He later became the 11th President of India (2002–2007) and is popularly called the 'Missile Man of India'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954.

• Kalam was born on 15 October 1931 at Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu; this day is observed as World Students' Day.

• He played a key role in Pokhran-II (1998) nuclear tests.

NOTE

• 1989 (Option 1): Not the year of his Bharat Ratna; no significance to his award.

• 2005 (Option 3): Falls during his post-Presidency period; not his award year.

• 2011 (Option 4): Incorrect year; he received the honour well before this.

question: In September 2024, who has been appointed as the new director general of the Narcotics Control Bureau?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anurag Garg.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In September 2024, senior IPS officer Anurag Garg took charge as the new Director General of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB).

• He is a 1993-batch IPS officer of the Himachal Pradesh cadre.

• The NCB (नारकोटिक्स कंट्रोल ब्यूरो) is the apex drug law-enforcement and intelligence agency in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The NCB was constituted in 1986 under the NDPS Act, 1985.

• It functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

• Its headquarters is in New Delhi.

NOTE

• Prakash Tomar (Option 1): Not associated with this NCB appointment.

• Nishant Sharma (Option 2): Not the appointed DG of NCB.

• Vikram Chaudhary (Option 4): Not the appointed DG of NCB.

question: In June 2025, which foreign brand unveiled footwear inspired by Kolhapuri chappals which sparked accusations of 'cultural misappropriation'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prada.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2025, the Italian luxury brand Prada unveiled sandals at its Milan show that closely resembled traditional Kolhapuri chappals, sparking accusations of 'cultural misappropriation'.

• Kolhapuri chappals (कोल्हापुरी चप्पल) are handcrafted leather footwear from Kolhapur, Maharashtra, and hold a GI (Geographical Indication) tag.

• Prada later acknowledged the Indian artisan heritage behind the design.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kolhapuri chappals received their GI tag in 2019, shared between Maharashtra and Karnataka.

• GI tags in India are governed under the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999.

• Prada is an Italian luxury fashion house founded in 1913.

NOTE

• Gucci (Option 2): An Italian luxury brand, but not the one linked to this controversy.

• Chanel (Option 3): A French luxury house, not involved here.

• Dior (Option 4): A French fashion brand, not involved in the Kolhapuri controversy.

question: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0, approved in August 2024 aims to provide housing subsidies to which group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Urban poor and middle-class families.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0), approved in August 2024, aims to provide housing assistance/subsidies to urban poor and middle-class families.

• It targets construction, purchase or rental of houses for eligible beneficiaries (शहरी गरीब और मध्यम वर्गीय परिवार).

• The scheme aims to build about one crore houses over five years.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• PMAY-U 2.0 is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

• It has four verticals: Beneficiary-Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS).

• The original PMAY was launched in 2015.

NOTE

• All women-headed households (Option 2): Not the defined target group of the scheme.

• MSME workers in urban slums (Option 3): Not the specific beneficiary category.

• Airline industry employees (Option 4): Unrelated to this housing scheme.

question: Which of the Indian state/union territory achieved 1st rank in India Electric Mobility Index 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Delhi secured the 1st rank in the India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI) 2024, released by NITI Aayog.

• The index was topped by Delhi, followed by Maharashtra and Chandigarh.

• The IEMI (भारत इलेक्ट्रिक मोबिलिटी सूचकांक) assesses states/UTs on their EV readiness and adoption.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The index evaluates parameters like EV adoption, charging infrastructure, and policy support.

• It was released alongside a report on India's USD 200 billion EV opportunity.

• NITI Aayog was established in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

NOTE

• Rajasthan (Option 2): Did not top the index.

• Lakshadweep (Option 3): A UT, but not the top ranker.

• Haryana (Option 4): Did not achieve the 1st rank.

question: The Kadbanwadi grassland is in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kadbanwadi grassland is located in Maharashtra, in the Pune district (Indapur region).

• It is a semi-arid grassland ecosystem (घास का मैदान) known for its biodiversity.

• It supports species such as the Indian wolf, blackbuck, foxes and various raptors.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Grasslands are important for grazing livestock and conserving open-country wildlife.

• Maharashtra's capital is Mumbai.

• The state is also known for grasslands and sanctuaries like Great Indian Bustard Sanctuary at Nannaj.

NOTE

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1): Known for shola grasslands in the Nilgiris, not Kadbanwadi.

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 2): Not the location of this grassland.

• Odisha (Option 3): Not associated with Kadbanwadi grassland.

question: Who is the author of the book 'The Namesake'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jhumpa Lahiri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'The Namesake' (2003) is a novel written by Jhumpa Lahiri, an Indian-American author.

• The novel explores the identity struggles of an Indian immigrant family in the United States (झुम्पा लाहिड़ी).

• It was later adapted into a film directed by Mira Nair in 2006.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Jhumpa Lahiri won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction (2000) for her debut short-story collection 'Interpreter of Maladies'.

• Her other works include 'The Lowland' and 'Unaccustomed Earth'.

• She was awarded the National Humanities Medal in the USA.

NOTE

• Arundhati Roy (Option 1): Author of 'The God of Small Things' (Booker Prize 1997).

• Satyajit Ray (Option 2): Legendary filmmaker and writer, creator of detective 'Feluda'.

• Arun Joshi (Option 4): Author of 'The Foreigner' and 'The Apprentice'.

question: 'Bengbung', a Mizo indigenous instrument, is similar to which instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Xylophone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Bengbung' is a Mizo indigenous musical instrument made of bamboo, played like and similar to a Xylophone (जाइलोफोन).

• It is a percussion/idiophone instrument, producing sound when struck with sticks.

• It is part of the traditional folk music of the Mizo tribe of Mizoram.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A xylophone consists of wooden bars struck by mallets to produce musical notes.

• Mizoram's other traditional instruments include the Khuang (drum) and Darkhuang (gong).

• Bamboo-based instruments are common in Northeast Indian folk traditions.

NOTE

• Flute (Option 1): A wind (aerophone) instrument, unlike the struck Bengbung.

• Cymbal (Option 2): A metallic clashing percussion instrument, different in form.

• Mridangam (Option 3): A South Indian double-headed drum used in Carnatic music.

question: Which traditional puppet dance of Tamil Nadu depicts scenes from the Ramayana and the Mahabharata?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bommalattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bommalattam is the traditional puppet dance/theatre of Tamil Nadu that depicts scenes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

• It combines features of rod and string puppetry (कठपुतली नृत्य).

• The puppets are among the largest and heaviest used in Indian puppetry.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other Indian puppet forms: Kathputli (Rajasthan), Gombeyatta (Karnataka), Ravanachhaya (Odisha) and Tholu Bommalata (Andhra Pradesh).

• Bommalattam is also known as Bommalattam / Bommalattam Koothu.

• Puppetry in India is broadly of four types: string, shadow, rod and glove puppets.

NOTE

• Ghotul (Option 1): A community/youth dormitory institution of the Muria Gond tribe, not a puppet dance.

• Parichakali (Option 2): A martial folk art form of Kerala.

• Bandiya (Option 3): Not a Tamil Nadu puppet dance form.

question: Which of the following is an example of artificial satellites? I. Sputnik-I II. GSAT-I
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both Sputnik-I and GSAT-I are examples of artificial satellites (कृत्रिम उपग्रह).

• Sputnik-I was the first artificial satellite, launched by the USSR in 1957.

• GSAT-I was a communication satellite launched by ISRO in 2001.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• An artificial satellite is a man-made object placed into orbit around Earth or another body.

• India's first satellite was Aryabhata (1975).

• INSAT and GSAT series are Indian communication satellites.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, since GSAT-I is also an artificial satellite.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, since Sputnik-I is also an artificial satellite.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both are artificial satellites.

question: What is the change of state from liquid to solid at atmospheric pressure known as?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Solidification.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The change of state from liquid to solid at atmospheric pressure is called solidification (also known as freezing).

• During solidification the substance releases heat (exothermic) (जमना).

• Example: water freezing into ice at 0°C.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Melting/Fusion: solid to liquid.

• Vaporisation: liquid to gas.

• Condensation: gas to liquid.

NOTE

• Deposition (Option 2): Direct change from gas to solid without becoming liquid.

• Sublimation (Option 3): Direct change from solid to gas (e.g., camphor, dry ice).

• Evaporation (Option 4): Change from liquid to gas at the surface below boiling point.

question: Which of the following is correct regarding law of conservation of energy? I. Energy can only be converted from one form to another. II. Energy can be easily destroyed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The law of conservation of energy (ऊर्जा संरक्षण का नियम) states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another.

• Hence statement I is correct and statement II is incorrect (energy cannot be destroyed).

• The total energy of an isolated system remains constant.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This law is a fundamental principle of physics/thermodynamics.

• Example: In a hydroelectric plant, potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy.

• The first law of thermodynamics is a statement of energy conservation.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Wrong, as energy cannot be easily destroyed.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong, because statement II is false.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Wrong, because statement I is true.

question: The 'ossification test' is used to determine the _____ of a person
solution_text:
The correct answer is Age.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ossification test is a medical/forensic test used to determine the approximate age of a person (आयु).

• It is based on the degree of fusion of bones and appearance of ossification centres seen through X-rays.

• It is commonly used in cases involving juveniles where age proof is unavailable.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ossification is the process of bone formation.

• Bones fully fuse by around the age of 25 years.

• The test uses X-rays of the wrist, elbow, shoulder, hip and knee joints.

NOTE

• Height (Option 2): Determined by direct measurement, not the ossification test.

• Weight (Option 3): Measured by weighing, unrelated to ossification.

• Blood group (Option 4): Determined by blood-type (ABO/Rh) tests.

question: In August 2025, which technological breakthrough aims to reduce India's reliance on Chinese specialty fertilisers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Water-soluble fertiliser process.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In August 2025, India developed its first indigenous water-soluble fertiliser (WSF) technology/process aimed at reducing reliance on Chinese specialty fertilisers imports.

• The water-soluble fertiliser process (जल में घुलनशील उर्वरक प्रक्रिया) helps make these fertilisers more affordable for farmers.

• Water-soluble fertilisers are used in drip irrigation and fertigation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India has been heavily dependent on imports of specialty and water-soluble fertilisers, largely from China.

• Water-soluble fertilisers dissolve completely in water and enhance nutrient use efficiency.

• Fertiliser subsidy in India is a major component of government expenditure.

NOTE

• Green hydrogen blend (Option 1): Relates to clean-energy fuel, not fertiliser imports.

• Nano-fertilizer deployment (Option 3): A different fertiliser innovation (e.g., nano-urea), not the referenced breakthrough.

• Fast-charging lithium battery process (Option 4): Related to EV batteries, unrelated to fertilisers.

question: In progressive income taxation _____.
option_1: higher income leads to a higher tax rate
option_2: everyone pays the same tax rate
option_3: lower income leads to a higher tax rate
option_4: higher income leads to a lower tax rate
solution_text:
The correct answer is higher income leads to a higher tax rate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under progressive income taxation (प्रगतिशील करारोपण), the tax rate increases as income increases, i.e., higher income leads to a higher tax rate.

• It is based on the principle of ability to pay, so the rich pay proportionately more.

• It helps in reducing income inequality.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India follows a progressive income tax system with income tax slabs.

• Regressive tax: rate decreases as income rises.

• Proportional tax: same rate regardless of income (flat tax).

NOTE

• everyone pays the same tax rate (Option 2): Describes a proportional/flat tax, not progressive.

• lower income leads to a higher tax rate (Option 3): Describes a regressive tax.

• higher income leads to a lower tax rate (Option 4): Also describes a regressive tax structure.

question: The code on social security extends social security to _____
solution_text:
The correct answer is organised or unorganised sector employee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Code on Social Security, 2020 extends social security benefits to workers in both the organised and unorganised sectors (संगठित या असंगठित क्षेत्र के कर्मचारी).

• It also covers gig workers and platform workers for the first time.

• It consolidates nine central labour laws relating to social security.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• It is one of the four labour codes enacted by India.

• It provides for benefits like EPF, ESI, gratuity, maternity benefit and pension.

• It proposes a National Social Security Board for unorganised workers.

NOTE

• only central government employee (Option 1): Too narrow; the code covers far more workers.

• only state government employee (Option 2): Incorrect and restrictive coverage.

• only private sector employee (Option 3): Incomplete, excludes unorganised/other workers.

question: Shivaji's exploits against which forces made him a legendary figure? I. Mughal II. Bijapur
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's exploits against both the Mughals and the Bijapur (Adil Shahi) Sultanate made him a legendary figure (मुगल और बीजापुर).

• He famously killed the Bijapur general Afzal Khan in 1659.

• He carried out a daring escape from Mughal captivity at Agra (1666) and challenged Aurangzeb.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674.

• He founded the Maratha Empire.

• He established an efficient administration with the council of ministers called Ashta Pradhan.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, ignores his campaigns against Bijapur.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, ignores his struggle against the Mughals.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as he fought both forces.

question: In which year the SEBI formulated the 'Insider Trading Regulations'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1992.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• SEBI formulated the Insider Trading Regulations in 1992 (SEBI (Insider Trading) Regulations, 1992).

• These regulations aim to prohibit trading in securities based on unpublished price-sensitive information.

• SEBI (भारतीय प्रतिभूति और विनिमय बोर्ड) was given statutory powers by the SEBI Act, 1992.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• SEBI was established in 1988 and got statutory status in 1992.

• The 1992 insider trading regulations were later replaced by the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015.

• SEBI's headquarters is in Mumbai.

NOTE

• 1996 (Option 1): Not the year the regulations were framed.

• 1990 (Option 2): SEBI did not yet have statutory backing then.

• 1994 (Option 4): Incorrect year for these regulations.

question: The Vice President of India can be removed from office by _____.
option_2: Resolution passed by the Council of States and agreed to by the House of the People
option_3: Resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament with one-thirds majority
option_4: The President on the advice of the Prime Minister
solution_text:
The correct answer is Resolution passed by the Council of States and agreed to by the House of the People.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vice President of India can be removed by a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha (House of the People).

• Such a resolution requires a 14 days' prior notice.

• This procedure is provided under Article 67(b) of the Constitution (भारत के उपराष्ट्रपति को हटाना).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

• Unlike the President, there is no formal 'impeachment' process and no specific grounds mentioned for his removal.

• The Vice President is elected by an electoral college of both Houses of Parliament.

NOTE

• Impeachment by the President (Option 1): Wrong; the VP is not removed by presidential impeachment.

• Resolution passed by both Houses with one-thirds majority (Option 3): Incorrect procedure and majority.

• The President on the advice of the Prime Minister (Option 4): Not the constitutional method of removal.

question: About what percentage of India's land are covered under plateau region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 27%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• About 27% of India's total land area is covered under the plateau region (पठारी क्षेत्र).

• Plateaus in India are rich in minerals like coal, iron ore and manganese.

• The major plateau is the Peninsular Plateau, one of the oldest landmasses.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's physiographic division: plains (~43%), mountains (~30%), plateaus (~27%).

• The Peninsular Plateau is divided into the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau.

• The Deccan Plateau is bordered by the Western and Eastern Ghats.

NOTE

• 5% (Option 1): Too low; underestimates plateau coverage.

• 12% (Option 2): Incorrect proportion for plateau region.

• 59% (Option 3): Too high; not the plateau share.

question: Land reforms introduced after the independence were successful in which of the following Indian state? I. Kerala II. West Bengal
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Post-independence land reforms (भू-सुधार) were notably successful in both Kerala and West Bengal.

• These states had strong Left/Communist governments that effectively implemented reforms.

• West Bengal's Operation Barga registered sharecroppers (bargadars) and protected their rights.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Land reform measures included abolition of intermediaries (zamindari), tenancy reforms, land ceilings and consolidation of holdings.

• Kerala passed the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

• Land reforms were aimed at redistributing land to the actual tillers.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as West Bengal was also successful.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as Kerala was also successful.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both states succeeded.

question: What was the share of industry in India's GDP in 1950-1951?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1950-51, the share of industry in India's GDP was about 13% (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद में उद्योग का हिस्सा).

• At independence, the Indian economy was predominantly agrarian, with agriculture contributing the largest share.

• Industrial development was later pushed through the Five Year Plans.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61), based on the Mahalanobis model, focused on heavy industries.

• The share of agriculture in GDP has steadily declined over decades while services have risen.

• Today the services sector contributes the largest share to India's GDP.

NOTE

• 5% (Option 1): Too low for the industry share in 1950-51.

• 7% (Option 2): Underestimates the industrial share.

• 27% (Option 4): Too high for that period.

question: In the context of population change, if the birth rate is _____ than death rate, the population will _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is more, be increase.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In population studies, if the birth rate is more than the death rate, the population will increase (जन्म दर मृत्यु दर से अधिक, जनसंख्या में बढ़ोतरी).

• The difference between birth rate and death rate is called the natural growth rate of population.

• A higher birth rate relative to death rate results in positive natural increase.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Birth rate = number of live births per 1,000 population per year.

• Death rate = number of deaths per 1,000 population per year.

• Population change also depends on migration (immigration and emigration).

NOTE

• more, be decrease (Option 2): Contradictory; higher births cannot reduce population.

• less, be increase (Option 3): Incorrect; a lower birth rate than death rate reduces population.

• less, remain same (Option 4): Incorrect; population would decline, not stay same.

question: In humans, what is the value of normal systolic and diastolic blood pressure respectively?
option_1: 75 mm Hg and 60 mm Hg respectively
option_2: 80 mm Hg and 70 mm Hg respectively
option_3: 100 mm Hg and 95 mm Hg respectively
option_4: 120 mm Hg and 80 mm Hg respectively
solution_text:
The correct answer is 120 mm Hg and 80 mm Hg respectively.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The normal systolic and diastolic blood pressure in a healthy human is about 120 mm Hg and 80 mm Hg respectively (120/80 mm Hg).

• Systolic pressure (प्रकुंचन) is measured when the heart contracts; diastolic pressure (अनुशिथिलन) when the heart relaxes.

• Blood pressure is measured using a sphygmomanometer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Blood pressure above 140/90 mm Hg is generally considered hypertension (high BP).

• Blood pressure below 90/60 mm Hg is termed hypotension (low BP).

• BP is expressed in millimetres of mercury (mm Hg).

NOTE

• 75 mm Hg and 60 mm Hg (Option 1): Below normal, indicating low blood pressure.

• 80 mm Hg and 70 mm Hg (Option 2): Not the standard normal values.

• 100 mm Hg and 95 mm Hg (Option 3): Abnormal, with a very high diastolic value.

question: In ancient India, the Mahajanapada of 'Anga' had its capital at which city in Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Champa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ancient Mahajanapada of 'Anga' had its capital at Champa, located in present-day Bihar (near Bhagalpur) (अंग महाजनपद की राजधानी चंपा).

• Champa was an important trade and commercial centre in ancient India.

• Anga was later annexed by Magadha under Bimbisara.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• There were 16 Mahajanapadas in ancient India (around the 6th century BCE).

• Champa was one of the six principal cities of ancient India mentioned in Buddhist texts.

• Magadha eventually became the most powerful Mahajanapada.

NOTE

• Vaishali (Option 1): Capital of the Vajji/Lichchhavi confederacy.

• Kausambi (Option 3): Capital of the Vatsa Mahajanapada.

• Gaya (Option 4): A religious city in Bihar, not the capital of Anga.
